primary_gt.decision_rule: Classify as temporary_snow_slowdown_residual_risk when residual_control_gap passes; snow_ends_incident requires residual_control_gap to fail.

criteria.description: Returns the requested compact JSON ledger and the final_state temporary_snow_slowdown_residual_risk.
criteria.name: final state and schema
criteria.partial_credit: Award 2-3 points for the correct state with missing fields; award 0-1 for snow_ends_incident or a choice-list answer.

criteria.description: Correctly computes the 140,000-acre increase, 5,833.3-acre-per-hour growth rate, 85 percent not contained, and 9.0-inch snow midpoint.
criteria.name: metric extraction and formulas
criteria.partial_credit: Award about 1 point per correct metric within tolerance; withhold credit for values copied without the required derived operation.

criteria.description: Applies the three inequalities correctly: growth rate > 5,000, not-contained share >= 80, and snow midpoint >= 6, yielding three pass flags.
criteria.name: threshold flags
criteria.partial_credit: Award 2-3 points for one wrong flag or minor inequality confusion; award 1 point for recognizing only the snow threshold.

criteria.description: Shows that the residual-control-gap pass blocks an incident-ending classification even though the snow-moderation test passes.
criteria.name: decision-rule proof
criteria.partial_credit: Award 2-3 points for the right conclusion without explicit rule logic; award 0-1 for treating snow magnitude alone as decisive.

criteria.description: Rejects snow_ends_incident or perimeter-only reasoning using the computed growth and containment thresholds.
criteria.name: rejected state
criteria.partial_credit: Award 1-2 points for rejecting the weaker state without citing both threshold anchors.

criteria.description: Uses units, reasonable rounding, and a one-sentence interpretation that stays within the computed threshold result.
criteria.name: precision and restraint
criteria.partial_credit: Award partial credit for a readable answer with minor rounding or wording issues.
